answer: A farm that wants 34 keys as a result pays 34 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the horizon seed, the pearl timing is verifiable from the wharf record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 318 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is inexpensive once and expensive in bulk. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
